newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Rep says $1.5 bln drawbridge plan acceptable.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Rep says $1.5 bln drawbridge plan acceptable.

text.p: A plan approved Thursday for construction of a $1.5 billion drawbridge linking Maryland and Virgina - part of which is likely to be paid by tax-exempt bonds - is a "step in the right direction," an aide to U.S. Rep. James Moran, D-Va., said Friday.
The proposed twelve lane, 70-foot-high toll bridge "is wider than what Moran wanted," the aide said. "But he's willing to work with the recommendation," the aide added.
A panel of state, local and federal officials narrowly approved the plan yesterday.

The span, which would cost motorists an estimated $1.30 in tolls each way, would replace the 35-year-old, deteriorating, six-lane Woodrow Wilson Bridge linking Alexandria, Va. and Prince George's County, Md.
"I think they will have to issue some kind of bonds because the only money available is the $410 million" that Congress is expected to kick in, Moran's aide said.
"The bridge will cost more than that (and) the interchanges are going to cost a lot more than that," the aide said. "You are going to see some borrowing," the aide said.
